name: Fortinet

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org - Wikipedia infobox logo file: Fortinet logo.svg

description: Fortinet sells network security built around its own chips and its FortiGate firewalls, sold as physical or virtual appliances, together with a stack of subscriptions (FortiGuard security updates) and support (FortiCare) that customers renew. It also sells secure networking (SD-WAN, switches, access points), cloud-delivered SASE and security-operations tools under one Security Fabric platform. Two thirds of revenue is service revenue (subscriptions and support recognised over time); one third is product sold once. Sales run mostly through channel partners to end-customers in over 100 countries, and the company owns much of its own data-center and office space (4.35M sq ft of owned facilities).

gics.note: Conventional label as listed in the Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' table (GICS sector and GICS sub-industry columns). That table does not give the industry group or industry levels, so they are null rather than filled from memory.

hq.note: 909 Kifer Road; about 395,000 sq ft on 21 acres (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Service (security subscriptions and support)
businessLines.how: Customers buy subscription and support contracts when they buy a firewall and renew them; the prepayment sits in deferred revenue and is recognised over the term.
businessLines.description: FortiGuard and other security subscriptions and FortiCare technical support.

businessLines.name: Product
businessLines.how: One-time sale of an appliance or licence through channel partners; management expects a multi-year firewall refresh cycle (10-K) which drives new subscription attach.
businessLines.description: Physical and virtual firewall and networking appliances plus software licences.
